queue.brief: On the 2026-08-28 restart the runner failed to launch a worker three times in a row (#34, #35, #36: 1–2 s, 0 tokens, rc=1, model '<synthetic>') and each failure BURNED a brief: run-loop.sh pops the brief before the worker starts, and on rc≠0 it backs off and pops the next one. Three planned briefs were destroyed without a worker ever reading them, and runlog/stall count the rows as ordinary failed iterations, so the dashboard reports 'src moved 7/10' for a run that shipped 7/7. Make a launch failure (rc≠0 with 0 tokens / no raw stream, or elapsed under ~30 s) leave the brief claimed and re-issue it on the next loop, and make stall.mjs and build-stats.mjs exclude such rows from verdict counts the way they already exclude manager rows. Second, smaller: motion.mjs sums a shower's rises and falls into one `jumps` figure, but only a FALL is the bug it exists for — split them so the night cell is attributable (was c62).
queue.successLooksLike: Simulating a launch failure (run the loop with a claude stub that exits 1 in 1 s) leaves current-brief.json claimed and RUNLOG.jsonl carries a row with kind 'launch-failed' that stall.mjs --report neither counts as a worker iteration nor as a verdict; the existing #34–36 rows are re-tagged the same way and the report reads shipped=7 for the last 7. motion.mjs prints rises and falls separately with the baseline regenerated.
queue.avoid: Do not touch courtyard.html. Do not delete the three synthetic rows — retag them; the archive is never edited away. Do not make the fix a retry loop inside run_claude: the runner already backs off on failure, the bug is only which brief the retry gets.

queue.brief: Every lit window in the town switches on in the same frame and off in the same frame. drawWindow() decides `lit` as `nightF > 0.3 && hash(sa*3, sb*7+day) > 0.42`, so roughly 58% of windows burn from dusk to dawn and nobody in this town goes to bed. Give each window its own hour: over a night the lit set should thin — early sleepers out by mid-evening, a few burning into the small hours, one or two coming on before dawn — so that 22.00 and 03.00 are visibly different pictures. Sky is ten iterations back and Sky x Polish is marked saturated; this is the deepening the domain actually wants. NOTE: this brief was issued at #34 and consumed by a harness fault before any worker ran (see b38) — there is no prior attempt to read.
queue.successLooksLike: A filmstrip cropped to the buildings across one night shows the lit count falling from an evening peak to a small-hours floor and lifting again before dawn, with no frame in which more than a couple of windows change at once. At nightF <= 0.3 nothing is lit, exactly as now, and the daytime frame is byte-identical to HEAD.
queue.avoid: LIT[] feeds the night glow pass — one predicate, one definition: whatever decides `lit` must be the same thing that pushes into LIT, or the glow and the pane disagree and only a crop will show it. Per-window variance comes from hash(), never R(): this runs in the renderer, and the renderer draws from the seeded stream. Match the grain — a window here is addressed per BUILDING per DAY, so a per-cell term is a silent no-op across a facade. And do not make it a second global scalar with a threshold; that is the switch you are replacing.

queue.brief: Nine systems read season() and every one of them is west of the bridge or in the sky. The plaza is identical in February and August — the exact position the market was in before #29. The fountain is the plaza’s landmark and has no seasonal reader at all. Give it the year: what the water does, what the basin looks like, and who is willing to stand near it should not be the same in midwinter as in midsummer. NOTE: issued at #35 and consumed by a harness fault before any worker ran — no prior attempt exists. Since #32 the bandstand DOES read the year (bandChance off warmth), so the plaza is now the only east-of-bridge place that does not.
queue.successLooksLike: A pinned midwinter and a pinned midsummer plaza differ visibly in the wide shot, and the difference is continuous — a probe over a folded year shows no step in the fountain terms at any phase, and every term reduces exactly to today’s constant at SEASON_START.
queue.avoid: riverRun() already exists for the water and reads the same year — read it or a sibling of it; do not re-derive a second water-season term (one predicate, one definition). Do not let a global scalar approach zero without per-cell variance or it reads as a switch. And check what the fountain was tuned against before making its constants variable: crumbSpot’s keep-rect reads waterBox off the grid, and #24 put 22 birds in the basin the last time two places evaluated the same geometry.

queue.brief: The allotment block is a vegetable block that does not contain only vegetables. The opening scatter seeds ornamentals into the plots — seed 42 opens with a fern in the block, seed 7 with a fern and a lavender — because speciesFor() filters only NEW sowing, not the initial scatter. Since #29 that matters in a way it did not before: harvestPlot() pays its cells into produce[], stockMarket() lays them out, and the town can now put a fern on a market stall as something a gardener grew to sell. Make the block vegetables from the first frame. NOTE: issued at #36 and consumed by a harness fault before any worker ran — no prior attempt exists.
queue.successLooksLike: Over ten seeds, no non-vegetable species ever occupies an allotment plot at t=0 or reaches mkShelf at any point in a folded year, and the courtyard beds are unchanged — the same eleven species in the same proportions as HEAD, proven against a stashed baseline.
queue.avoid: Do not fix it by filtering at the market — that is a second predicate for what an allotment grows and it will drift from speciesFor(). Fix it where the block is populated. Expect the census to churn everywhere: any change to the opening scatter reshuffles the seeded world, so read the diff for collapse, not delta.

queue.brief: nameAt(x,y) names the ground, the plants, the plots, the waters and the thirteen trees — and nothing that MOVES. Point at a walker, a duck, a swan, the sweeper, a gardener with a basket, the rowboat, the concert audience or the cat, and the sill says the paving under their feet. Since #33 the living things are the most legible part of a night frame. __entities() already carries role, act and a stable id per person, and crowns[] is the pattern for hit-testing a moving thing in SCREEN space. Give the pointer the living things, with the same NAME_SETTLE hold as everything else, and let the name say what they are DOING ('someone waiting at the door', 'a swan, upending') rather than only what they are.
queue.successLooksLike: probes/naming.mjs extended: over ten seeds, pointing at the screen position of any agent, duck, swan or the boat returns a living name at least 95% of the time and NEVER the paving, and pointing at a spot 2 cells clear of every entity still returns exactly what HEAD returns. A moving figure holds its name for NAME_SETTLE after it walks out from under the pointer, no flicker.
queue.avoid: Hit-test in screen space against the drawn footprint (project() the feet, a box of roughly 0.9 cells) — never re-derive world geometry, and never add an R() draw: the renderer walks the seeded stream. The sill is DOM and fails quietly: assert on computed text, not on the handler having run. Do not add a new invitation for it; OFFERS[] is the queue and the naming already has its hint.
